verdict: Spend collapsed to $3.85 in the latest period with no lead or conversion data to judge results.
diagnosis: Total spend of $2,330 over 28 days ran a single PCOS and postpartum lead campaign, but no lead volume or pipeline data is available.

signals.headline: Spend dropped to $3.85 latest day
signals.detail: Daily spend fell far below the $13.63 period average, suggesting a paused or budget-capped campaign.

signals.headline: Only 1 active campaign running
signals.detail: The PCOS and postpartum persona campaign is the sole line item, creating single-point-of-failure risk.

signals.headline: $2,330 spent, 0 leads reported
signals.detail: No lead, conversion, or pipeline data feeds through, making cost per lead impossible to calculate.

signals.headline: 0 organic or local signals tracked
signals.detail: Google Business Profile, organic social, and CRM are all blank, hiding whether ads are producing calls or bookings.

benchmark.label: Benchmark
benchmark.body: Boutique and personal training studios typically see Facebook cost per lead between $32 and $52, with the fitness category averaging around $29.70. Fitness lead form conversion rates lead all industries near 14%.

seasonal.label: Seasonal
seasonal.body: Facebook cost per thousand impressions for fitness hit a yearly high of $29.68 in July 2026, up 44% from June. August historically stays elevated before a Q4 lull.

competitor.label: Competitor
competitor.subheader: Studios pivoting to retention and Pilates
competitor.body: Boutique studios are shifting budget from acquisition toward community, retention, and Pilates or reformer formats. Cancellations dropped 6% at studios last year while gyms rose 8%.

recommendations.title: Connect lead tracking before spending more
recommendations.detail: Consider wiring Facebook lead form submissions and CRM data into reporting. Without lead counts, the $2,330 spent this period cannot be judged against the $32–$52 studio benchmark.

recommendations.title: Investigate the spend drop to $3.85
recommendations.detail: Worth checking whether the campaign hit a budget cap, was paused, or lost delivery. Late-August ad auctions are competitive, so silence here likely means missed leads.

recommendations.title: Test a second campaign angle beyond PCOS and postpartum
recommendations.detail: Consider adding a broader women's strength or Pilates angle. A single persona campaign concentrates risk, and category momentum favors low-impact and community-led formats.
